Definition: from κίω (poetic for εἶμι, to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively:--(re-)move(-r), way.
KeyPassages: Matthew 23:4; Matthew 27:39; Mark 15:29; Acts 17:28; Acts 21:30; Revelation 2:5
BiblicalUsage: Kineo means to stir, to move. Matthew 23:4 says the Pharisees will not move heavy burdens with one of their fingers, Matthew 27:39 and Mark 15:29 have the passers-by wagging their heads at the crucified Jesus, and Acts 21:30 says all the city was moved when Paul was seized in the temple. Acts 17:28 turns the word toward God: in him we live, and move, and have our being. Revelation 2:5 warns the church at Ephesus that Christ will remove its candlestick unless it repents.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe kineo runs both ways: men move their heads in mockery and cities move in rage, but we live and move in God. I hold that the only moving that matters is the one in Acts 17:28, because a candlestick can be removed and a city can be stirred, but in Him we have our being.
